title: What Is The Biggest Threat To Microsoft Stock? - Trefis
content: Buyers are paying for growth, and Microsoft (MSFT) is delivering it. The stock returned 37.2% between July 17 and October 15, 2026, against 4.1% for the S&P 500. Revenue climbed 17.7% in fiscal Q4 2026 from a year earlier. Yet on a July 29 earnings call, executives described a cost to that growth that is still rising. What is that cost, and who is raising it? The cost is the AI capacity Microsoft is building, and the company’s executives raised it on that same call. Customer demand still exceeds the capacity Microsoft has available, management said. In July, the company expected to spend over $50 billion on capital in fiscal Q1 2027, covering the July to September quarter. This figure includes the effect of a change in how it counts some leases. Microsoft also expects capital spending for fiscal 2027 as a whole to grow from the year before. That heavy spending already shows in Microsoft’s financial results. Gross margin was 67.2% in fiscal Q4 2026, against 68.6% a year earlier. Management attributed this decline to a shift in sales toward Azure and to continued investment in AI infrastructure. Free cash flow, the cash left after that spending, fell to $19.6 billion from $25.6 billion a year earlier, even as cash from operations rose. Microsoft’s Intelligent Cloud segment brought in $39.3 billion in fiscal Q4 2026. This accounted for more than two-fifths of the company’s revenue and represented 32% growth from a year earlier. No other Microsoft segment grew as fast during that quarter, and revenue in Azure and other cloud services grew 43%. Microsoft is building capacity to keep up with precisely this growth. At today’s price, there is little room for that spending to disappoint. Microsoft stock trades at 30.0 times its earnings over the past twelve months, against 22.7 for the S&P 500. At the end of June, the same earnings were priced at 20.7 times, the lowest at any quarter end since fiscal 2017. On October 15, the shares closed less than 1% below their highest close of the past year. The current stock price appears to assume the spending will pay off. Microsoft shareholders face a real but slow risk. Operating margin was 45.1% in fiscal Q4 2026, against 44.9% a year earlier, meaning Microsoft still keeps a slightly larger share of its sales as operating profit. For fiscal 2027 as a whole, management expects operating margin to be down less than 1 point, even as the company invests to meet growing demand. So far, the cost shows up in Microsoft’s cash and its gross margin, while operating margin has held steady. Free cash flow is the key metric to watch in Microsoft’s next report, which will cover the July to September quarter. content: Ni Source inc. (NI) shares were in focus on Friday after the utility announced a long-term energy agreement with Microsoft (MSFT) for its planned northwest Indiana campus. Its new 20-year agreement for the planned campus is expected to contribute to a broader strategy that NiSource says could deliver $1.75 billion in savings to existing electricity customers. “Affordability is not separate from economic development; it is a key pillar of our GenCo model,” NiSource CEO Lloyd Yates said, adding that the company aims to attract investment and create jobs while protecting existing customers. The agreement raises total expected savings for Northern Indiana Public Service Company (NIPSCO) electric customers could be approximately $1.75 billion over the life of data-center customer contracts, up from the previously announced $1.4 billion. NiSource estimates the savings could amount to as much as $140 per customer annually. According to NiSource, Microsoft will fully fund the generation and transmission infrastructure required to serve its electricity demand. The company said the infrastructure will also upgrade NIPSCO’s electric transmission system, with the aim of improving grid reliability and resilience while protecting existing residential and business customers from the costs of serving the data center. GenCo has also contracted 600 MW of battery storage under a long-term tolling agreement. An affiliate of AGP Group will develop and construct the facility, which will become part of GenCo’s resource pool serving multiple large-load customers. Riles added that the partnership with NIPSCO is intended to support growth, protect ratepayers and help maintain a reliable grid for communities in northern Indiana. Zhitong Finance APP learned that the UK's Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) said Friday that Microsoft's (MSFT.US) control over business software is making it harder for customers to switch vendors, and therefore proposed imposing stricter regulations on the tech giant. The CMA stated it will decide by February next year whether to designate Microsoft as having "strategic market power." title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella Just Shared Bad News for Nvidia and Great News for This Rival Chipmaker - The Motley Fool
content: New plans for Azure could leave less room for Nvidia. Microsoft (MSFT -1.93%) is planning a big change to its Azure cloud computing data centers starting next year. It will rely much more on its custom-designed silicon than on leading graphics processing units (GPUs) like those from Nvidia (NVDA -1.43%). It's already made significant progress in expanding workloads for its Maia 200 chips, and it expects its next-generation Maia 300 chips to deliver significant improvements when it starts deploying them next year. "Starting next calendar year, we will scale our Maia family to multi-gigawatt deployments, making it the primary inference system for our own product and services," CEO Satya Nadella said.  That's great news for its custom chip partner, Marvell Technology (MRVL -5.56%), and bad news for Nvidia. Nvidia's extreme dominance of the data center GPU space during the first few years of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom left its market share with nowhere to go but down. Its biggest customers, including the hyperscalers and leading AI frontier labs, have developed custom solutions that can handle AI workloads, and that can deliver better price performance on specific tasks than Nvidia's GPUs. That said, GPUs offer far greater flexibility in terms of the types of tasks they can perform, making them particularly valuable for companies deploying servers to sell compute capacity to third parties with dynamic demands. Notice that Microsoft is starting its Maia expansion by focusing on its own products and services, not on leasing Maia compute capacity to third parties looking to cut costs on their OpenAI GPT-based applications. Their use, though, could expand over the long run. Alphabet (GOOG -2.32%) (GOOGL -2.47%), which has been building its own custom AI chips for longer than any of its competitors, has seen strong adoption of its Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) by its Google Cloud customers for training and inference. Apple used TPUs to train Apple Intelligence, and Anthropic is using gigawatts worth of TPUs to develop its large language models. While Nvidia can continue to grow sales extremely quickly, other chipmakers' growth rates are likely to outpace it. Its work on the Maia 300 is likely a big reason why. Microsoft's plan to make that processor the primary inference system for its products and services is in line with earlier reports that it will make a big step up in custom silicon orders starting next year. The revenue opportunity for Marvell is huge. Microsoft will spend approximately $175 billion in capital expenditures on data centers over the next year. Roughly two-thirds of that will go toward servers and networking equipment. If Marvell takes just a sliver of that spending, it would amount to a huge boost to its revenue, which totaled just $9.5 billion over the last four quarters. Marvell believes the combination of its custom AI chips and its networking chips will help it grow revenue tenfold over the next five years. title: Dan Ives Believes MSFT Is The Most Oversold Large-Cap Stock, Draws Parallels To 'Negative' Narratives Around GOOGL A Year Ago - Stocktwits
content: Wedbush’s Global Head of Tech Research, Dan Ives, on Wednesday said that Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) is the most oversold large-cap stock. During an interview with Bloomberg, Ives highlighted Microsoft’s potential despite some missteps with Copilot, its AI companion. "Have they made stumbles on Copilot and some other areas? Yeah. But in terms of enterprise, their backyard... Azure growth, compute supply issues... I think that that's ultimately a stock that, you know, $550, so I actually think that continues,” he said. Microsoft shares were down about 1% in Wednesday’s pre-market trade. Ives drew parallels between the existing narrative around Microsoft to the conversations around Alphabet Inc.’s (GOOG, GOOGL) Google a year ago. “Just like a year ago, the narrative on Google was so negative,” he said. Alphabet’s Class A shares fell about 18% in the first quarter (Q1) last year. The company revamped its AI strategy in April 2025, tasking veteran Josh Woodward with leading Gemini amid concerns about AI eating into its search business. Since then, GOOGL stock is up about 138%. Ives said that there are no cracks in the AI armor despite the recent selloff in tech, AI and chip stocks, citing the firm’s channel checks in Taiwan and South Korea. He added that currently, demand for AI infrastructure is outstripping supply by a ratio of 15 to 1. “My view is, even if you had some events to take some demand off, you don’t have an equilibrium probably for another year and half or two years,” he added, while saying that chip trade is what investors should continue to own. Ives added that even if margin pressures begin to show up, he doesn’t see them reflecting in companies’ earnings for the next nine to 12 months. “In my view, it just continues to be like… we’re still so early, relative to the [AI] buildout. You’re going to have these gut check moments, you’ll have these white knuckle periods, but we continue to view these as opportunities where you own the AI winners,” he added. MSFT stock is down 23% year-to-date, while GOOGL stock is up 11%. The S&P 500 ETF (SPY) is up 22% over the past 12 months, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) is up 34%. A key provision in the crypto industry’s closely watched market structure bill is facing fresh resistance ahead of a planned Senate vote next month. A coalition of major law enforcement organizations urged the Trump administration to reconsider a key developer-protection provision in the CLARITY Act, arguing it could create oversight gaps and complicate efforts to investigate illicit finance. The criticism centers around Section 604 of the CLARITY Act, which is also known as the Blockchain Regulatory Certainty Act (BRCA). The law enforcement groups representing prosecutors, sheriffs, police chiefs, and officers sent a letter to Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche and White House crypto adviser Patrick Witt expressing concerns about Section 604 of the CLARITY Act, journalist Eleanor Terrett reported on Tuesday. The section of the bill in question, Section 604, tackles the regulatory framework for digital asset service providers, with the goal of protecting non-controlling developers, open-source contributors, self-custodial tools, and specific decentralized finance (DeFi) infrastructure from being automatically classed as money transmitters. According to the letter, the four groups, including the National Sheriffs' Association, National Association of Assistant US Attorneys, National District Attorneys Association, and International Association of Chiefs of Police, argued that the provision could create gaps in accountability, hinder investigations into illicit activity, and potentially exempt some crypto participants from certain know your customer (KYC) and anti-money-laundering (AML) reporting requirements. On Tuesday, a coalition of Catholic organizations and anti-human-trafficking advocates named The Alliance to End Human Trafficking (AEHT) urged Senate leadership to oppose the BRCA provision, arguing it could weaken safeguards against illicit finance and create loopholes for traffickers and transnational criminal organizations. In the letter, the organization challenged arguments from crypto advocacy groups that the provision is necessary to protect non-custodial developers, open-source software projects, and blockchain infrastructure providers from being treated as money transmitters. Despite the criticism, the law enforcement opposition did not appear unanimous. Terrett said that the Grand Lodge Fraternal Order of Police (GLFOP) and the National Association of Police Organizations (NAPO), two major law enforcement groups involved in discussions about the legislation, did not sign the letter. The latest objections added another point of contention to Senate negotiations over the CLARITY Act, alongside the ongoing debate over ethics provisions related to President Donald Trump's family's crypto businesses. Supporters of the provision argue that writing code should not, by itself, trigger money-transmitter obligations. Sen. Cynthia Lummis (R-Wyo.), one of the bill's leading advocates, reiterated that position on Tuesday, writing that "The Clarity Act is clear: writing code is not money transmission. That distinction will matter for a generation of builders." Republicans have been targeting a Senate floor vote on the CLARITY Act on July 17, after lawmakers return from the July 4 recess, though negotiations over ethics provisions, developer protections, and other outstanding issues remain ongoing. He added that initiatives, including Network 2.0, the Tricolor strategy, and operational improvements in Europe, helped drive productivity gains. Those efforts enabled FedEx to surpass its previously announced target of $1 billion in transformation-related savings during the fiscal year. “We remain firmly on track to achieve our Investor Day commitments for 2029 with clear proof points in the quarter. B2B services drove the majority of our quarterly revenue growth supporting high profit flow-through, " Subramaniam said. FedEx completed the spin-off of FedEx Freight on June 1. Subramaniam said the separation will allow both companies to operate independently and focus on growing their own core businesses. FedEx stock traded over 6% lower in Wednesday’s premarket.
